title: Paramartha Guru Tale 60

full_text:
The regional temple possessed a magnificent, ancient granite gopuram tower that soared one hundred and twenty cubits into the sky, adorned with thousands of carved figures of celestial dancers, lions, and deities.

The village council was debating the exact height of the tower to order new copper flagpoles, but no carpenter was brave enough to climb to the dizzying pinnacle with a measuring cord.

Guru Paramartha offered his services: 'A philosopher does not risk his neck upon heights; he measures the tower through its projected shadow upon the earth!'

The village elders praised his wisdom and promised ten silver rupees for the measurement.

At seven o'clock in the morning, when the sun was low on the eastern horizon, the temple gopuram cast an enormous, colossal, elongated shadow that stretched three hundred paces across the western fields, over a fence, and into a farmer's cabbage patch.

Matti and Madayan arrived with a bamboo measuring pole.

Matti began measuring the shadow from the base of the tower: 'One pole... two poles... ten poles...'

Because the sun was rising steadily in the sky, the shadow was shrinking every minute!

By the time Matti reached the cabbage patch, the tip of the shadow had retreated fifty paces toward the temple!

Matti shouted in bewilderment: 'Madayan! The shadow is retreating! It is running backward toward the tower!'

Madayan checked his calculations: 'The tower is shrinking! As the morning heat increases, the granite stones are contracting into the earth! Measure faster before the tower disappears completely!'

The two disciples ran back and forth across the fields, chasing the shrinking shadow like boys chasing butterflies!

By noon, the sun was directly overhead. The shadow shrank to a tiny, two-foot pool of shade huddled directly beneath the eaves of the foundation.

Matti stood beside the foundation, measured the two-foot shadow with his hand, and reported in triumph: 'Master! The tower is exactly two cubits high!'

Guru Paramartha delivered his official report to the village council: 'Honorable elders, your colossal temple tower is exactly two cubits in height; an ordinary goat can step over it with ease!'

The village elders stared at the soaring, one-hundred-and-twenty-cubit stone tower, then at the Guru's report, and burst into roaring laughter!

The chief elder said: 'If our tower is two cubits high, O wise Guru, why do your eyes water when you look up at the top?'

The Guru replied with unruffled dignity: 'Optical refraction, elder; the tower is small, but the air above it is remarkably magnified!'
moral: Chasing a shifting shadow to measure a permanent tower leaves you wandering in the fields.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Paramartha Guru Tale 60"?
options: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
